alt: Boules steel balls lawn game rental
name: Boules
blurb: Played between two teams, participants throw or roll steel balls as close as possible to the target jack.
includes: Carry bag with 8 patterned steel balls, jack, and measuring string.
title: Boules (Pétanque) Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire a boules (pétanque) set for events in Pretoria, Johannesburg or Gauteng. Eight steel balls, jack and measuring string. R250 plus refundable deposit.
intro: Boules - also known as pétanque or bocce - is the game you'll see played in French village squares: teams take turns throwing steel balls as close as they can to a small target ball, the jack. It's slow-paced, sociable and easy to pick up with a drink in the other hand, which makes it one of the most popular choices for wedding receptions and garden parties.
The set is the real thing: eight patterned steel boules, a wooden jack and a measuring string for settling close calls.
players: 2 to 8 (singles, pairs or teams of three)
surface: Any flat ground - gravel, paving or short grass. Long grass slows the balls down.
weather: Unaffected by wind. Fine in light drizzle; dry the balls before packing.
rules: One player tosses the jack 6 to 10 metres from the throwing circle.
Teams take turns throwing or rolling their boules toward the jack. The team whose boule is furthest from the jack throws next.
Once all boules are thrown, the end is scored: the team closest to the jack scores one point for every boule closer than the opponent's best.
Use the measuring string for anything too close to call.
The winning team throws the next jack. First to 13 points wins.
faqs: Can boules be played on paving or a patio?
Yes. It's traditionally played on gravel, so any hard, flat surface works well. Grass is fine too as long as it's short.
How many people can play at once?
Up to eight, with two balls each in teams. Larger groups simply rotate in - an end takes only a few minutes.

alt: Cornhole board bean bag lawn game rental
name: Cornhole
blurb: Classic lawn game where players alternate throwing bean bags toward a raised platform with a target hole.
includes: Carry case, 2 boards, and 2 sets of bean bags (4 per color).
title: Cornhole (Bean Bag Toss) Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire a cornhole set, two boards and eight bean bags, for weddings, parties and corporate events in Pretoria and Johannesburg. R250 plus deposit.
intro: Cornhole is the American backyard classic: players take turns tossing bean bags at a raised wooden board, aiming for the hole. It's the easiest game on our list to explain, takes two minutes to set up, and gets competitive surprisingly quickly.
The set comes in its own carry case with two boards and two sets of four bean bags in contrasting colours.
space: Roughly 3 × 10 m with the boards 8 m apart; move them closer for children
surface: Any flat ground, indoors or out.
weather: Bean bags catch in strong wind. Keep them dry - they're fabric.
rules: Set the two boards facing each other, about 8 metres apart (front edge to front edge).
Players stand beside their board and alternate throwing their four bags at the opposite board.
A bag through the hole scores 3 points; a bag resting on the board scores 1.
Scores cancel each round - if you score 4 and your opponent scores 3, you get 1.
First player or team to 21 points wins.
faqs: Is cornhole suitable for children?
Very. Just move the boards closer together - 4 or 5 metres apart works well for younger children.
Can it be played indoors?
Yes. The boards sit flat on any floor, and the bean bags won't damage anything.

name: Croquet
blurb: A traditional sport involving hitting wooden balls through hoops embedded in a lawn court.
includes: Carry bag with 6 hoops, 4 wooden mallets, 4 balls, and booklet.
title: Croquet Set Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire a full croquet set with six hoops, four mallets and balls for garden weddings and events in Pretoria and Johannesburg. R400 plus deposit.
intro: Croquet is the game that belongs on a lawn at a garden wedding. Players knock wooden balls through a course of hoops with a mallet, and the strategy - knocking opponents out of position - is where it gets entertaining. It's unhurried, it photographs beautifully, and guests in formal wear can play it without breaking a sweat.
This is one of our two Big games: a full set with six hoops, four wooden mallets, four balls and a rules booklet, in a carry bag.
players: 2 to 4 with the set; larger groups play in pairs
space: Ideally 10 × 15 m of lawn; a smaller course works fine in a compact garden
surface: Grass only - the hoops push into the ground.
duration: 30 to 60 minutes for a full course
weather: Unaffected by wind. Wet grass is playable but slows the balls.
rules: Push the six hoops into the lawn in a course, with the peg in the centre. The booklet shows the standard layout.
Each player takes a mallet and a ball, and plays in colour order from the starting line.
Hit your ball through the hoops in sequence. Passing through a hoop earns you an extra shot.
Hitting another player's ball (a roquet) also earns extra shots - and lets you knock their ball out of position.
The first player to complete all the hoops and hit the centre peg wins.
faqs: Does croquet need a perfectly flat lawn?
No. A reasonably level, short-mown lawn is all it takes. Bumps add character; long grass is the only real problem.
Can more than four people play?
The set has four balls, so play in pairs or rotate players between games. Teams of two work well and keep everyone involved.

alt: Giant 4 in a Row connection game rental
name: Giant 4 in a Row
blurb: Two-player connection game to form a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four chips.
includes: Freestanding wooden board with 48 colored chips and setup guide.
title: Giant 4 in a Row (Connect 4) Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire giant 4 in a Row, a freestanding Connect-4-style board with 48 chips, for events in Pretoria, Johannesburg and Gauteng. R250 plus deposit.
intro: Giant 4 in a Row is the oversized, freestanding version of Connect 4: two players take turns dropping coloured chips into the frame, racing to line up four. Games last a couple of minutes, so a queue forms and moves quickly - it's the game we'd put nearest the bar.
The board stands on its own on any flat surface, and the chips release with a slide of the bottom bar for an instant reset.
players: 2 at a time, with a crowd watching
surface: Any flat surface, indoors or out.
weather: Fine in a breeze; move it under cover in strong wind.
rules: Each player takes a colour - 24 chips each.
Take turns dropping one chip into any column. It falls to the lowest empty slot.
The first player to line up four chips in a row - horizontally, vertically or diagonally - wins.
If the board fills with no line of four, it's a draw.
Slide the release bar to empty the board and play again.
faqs: Can giant 4 in a Row be used indoors?
Yes. It's freestanding and doesn't need to be anchored, so it works in a marquee, hall or on a patio.
Is it suitable for young children?
One of the best games for them - the rules take ten seconds to explain, and the chips are large enough for small hands.

name: Giant Dominoes
blurb: Traditional domino rules scaled up for group outdoor play and team matches.
includes: Carry case with 28 oversized wooden dominoes.
title: Giant Dominoes Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire 28 giant wooden dominoes for garden parties, weddings and team events across Pretoria, Johannesburg and Gauteng. R250 plus refundable deposit.
intro: Giant dominoes are the classic game scaled up for the garden: 28 oversized wooden tiles, big enough to play on the lawn and satisfying to set up in a toppling run when the game's over. It's a gentle, all-ages option that grandparents and toddlers can play together.
The full double-six set comes in its own carry case.
space: A 2 × 2 m area on the ground or a long table
weather: Unaffected by wind - the tiles are heavy.
rules: Shuffle the dominoes face down. Each player draws seven (two players) or five (three or four players).
The player holding the highest double lays it first.
Take turns adding a domino to either end of the line, matching the number of dots.
If you can't play, draw from the pile until you can. If the pile is empty, pass.
The first player to lay all their dominoes wins the round, scoring the dots left in everyone else's hand.
faqs: Do giant dominoes need a table?
No. They play just as well on a lawn or patio - the tiles are big enough to read from standing height.
Are they good for children's parties?
Yes, and not only for the game: children love standing them up in a line and toppling them.

name: Giant Pick-up Sticks
blurb: Test of physical dexterity and focus to remove sticks from a random pile without disturbance.
includes: Carry bag with 30 colorful wooden pick-up sticks.
title: Giant Pick-up Sticks Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire giant pick-up sticks, 30 colourful wooden sticks, for parties and events in Pretoria, Johannesburg and Gauteng. R150 plus refundable deposit.
intro: Giant pick-up sticks (Mikado) is a test of nerves: drop the bundle, then take turns lifting one stick out without disturbing any other. At this scale - 30 sticks nearly a metre long - the tension is real, and it draws a crowd of people holding their breath.
Sticks are colour-coded for scoring and come in a carry bag.
surface: Any flat surface - lawn, deck or floor.
weather: Play out of strong wind, which can shift the sticks.
rules: One player holds the bundle upright, then lets go so the sticks fall in a heap.
Take turns removing a single stick without moving any other. You may use a stick you've already won as a tool.
If any other stick moves, your turn ends and the next player goes.
Each colour is worth a different number of points - the rarest colour scores highest.
When all sticks are taken, the highest total wins.
faqs: How is giant pick-up sticks scored?
By colour. Assign each colour a value before you start - the set's rarest colour is traditionally worth the most.
Can it be played indoors?
Yes, on any floor with a couple of metres of space.

alt: High Tower wooden stacking game rental
name: High Tower
blurb: A game of structural balance where players take turns pulling blocks to build an unstable tower.
includes: Convertible carry case/stand with 48 wooden blocks.
title: High Tower (Giant Jenga) Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire High Tower, our giant Jenga-style stacking game with 48 solid wooden blocks, for events in Pretoria and Johannesburg. R400 plus deposit.
intro: High Tower is our giant Jenga-style stacking game, and it's the one guests remember. Players take turns pulling a wooden block from the tower and placing it on top, and the tower grows taller and less stable until someone brings it down. The crash is half the fun.
One of our two Big games. The 48 solid wooden blocks travel in a case that converts into the stand the tower is built on, so it starts at a comfortable height.
ages: 6 and up, with an adult nearby - the blocks are heavy
space: About 1.5 × 1.5 m, with room to stand clear when it falls
surface: Firm and level: paving, decking or hard flat lawn. Soft or sloping ground makes the tower unsteady.
weather: Not in strong wind - a tall tower catches it.
rules: Build the tower on the stand: three blocks per layer, each layer at right angles to the one below, until all 48 are stacked.
Take turns removing any one block from below the top completed layer, using one hand.
Place the block on top of the tower to start a new layer.
You may touch blocks to find a loose one, but must put back any you don't take.
The player who topples the tower loses. Rebuild and go again.
faqs: How tall does High Tower get?
It starts at knee height on its stand and grows past a metre as blocks move to the top. Clear a space around it - it comes down with a satisfying crash.
Is High Tower safe for children?
Yes with an adult nearby. The blocks are solid wood and heavy; toes and small fingers should stay clear of the landing zone.

name: Horseshoe Throwing
blurb: Outdoor target sport played between two people pitching horseshoes toward ground stakes.
includes: Carry bag, 4 horseshoes, 2 rubber mats, and 4 stakes.
title: Horseshoe Throwing Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire a horseshoe throwing set with four horseshoes, stakes and mats for garden parties and events in Pretoria and Johannesburg. R150 plus deposit.
intro: Horseshoe throwing is the farmyard original: pitch a horseshoe at a stake and try to ring it. It's a simple, satisfying throwing game with a bit of a knack to it, and the clang of a ringer carries across a party.
The set includes four horseshoes, four stakes and two rubber mats, so it can be played on paving as well as grass.
ages: 8 and up - the horseshoes are metal
space: A lane of roughly 3 × 12 m, with the stakes 8 to 12 m apart
surface: Grass or sand; the mats let it go on paving too.
rules: Set two stakes (or mats) facing each other, 8 to 12 metres apart - closer for beginners.
Players pitch two horseshoes each per turn from beside one stake toward the other, throwing one at a time.
A ringer - the horseshoe encircling the stake - scores 3 points. The closest horseshoe within a shoe's width scores 1.
Only the better-placed horseshoes count each turn; equal ringers cancel.
First to 21 wins, or play to 15 for a quicker game.
faqs: Is horseshoe throwing safe at a party?
Yes with basic care: throw one at a time, and nobody stands near the target stake while shoes are in the air. We'd keep it for ages 8 and up.
Can it be played on paving?
Yes. The two rubber mats included in the set hold the stakes, so no soft ground is needed.

name: Lawn Darts
blurb: Aerodynamically stable darts thrown over a distance into target rings to score points.
includes: Carry case with 4 lawn darts and 3 scoring rings.
title: Lawn Darts Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire a lawn darts set with four weighted darts and three scoring rings for garden events in Pretoria, Johannesburg and Gauteng. R150 plus deposit.
intro: Lawn darts is a gentle underarm throwing game: lob the large, finned darts so they land inside the scoring rings laid out on the grass. It's easy for anyone to try, quick to set up, and takes almost no space.
The set comes in a carry case with four lawn darts and three scoring rings.
surface: Grass - the darts land tip-first and need to stand up.
weather: Wind affects the flight, so choose a sheltered spot on a gusty day.
rules: Lay the scoring rings on the grass 5 to 8 metres from the throwing line.
Take turns lobbing your darts underarm so they arc up and land point-first.
Score by the ring the dart lands in - the smallest ring scores most.
Darts that land outside all rings score nothing.
First to 21 points wins.
faqs: Are lawn darts safe?
These are the modern rounded-tip type, not the sharp metal darts banned years ago. Throw underarm, one at a time, and keep the landing area clear.
Can lawn darts be played on hard ground?
They're designed for grass, where the tip settles into the lawn. On paving they bounce and won't score reliably.

alt: Noughts and Crosses tic-tac-toe lawn game
name: Noughts and Crosses
blurb: Classic Tic-Tac-Toe played on a large modular rope grid layout.
includes: Carry bag featuring 5 noughts, 5 crosses, and rope grid.
title: Giant Noughts & Crosses (Tic Tac Toe) Hire | Gauteng
description: Hire giant noughts and crosses, a rope grid with wooden pieces, for kids' parties and events in Pretoria and Johannesburg. R150 plus deposit.
intro: Giant noughts and crosses - tic tac toe - is the simplest game we hire, and for a children's party that's exactly the point. Lay the rope grid on the grass, hand out the wooden pieces, and even the youngest guests can play unsupervised.
The set includes five noughts, five crosses and a modular rope grid, in a carry bag.
rules: Lay out the rope grid to make nine squares.
One player takes the noughts, the other the crosses.
Take turns placing a piece in an empty square.
Three in a row - across, down or diagonally - wins.
If all nine squares fill with no line, it's a draw. Clear and play again.
faqs: Is it suitable for toddlers?
Yes - it's the one game on our list a three-year-old can play. The pieces are large, light and safe.
Can it be played indoors?
Yes. The rope grid lies flat on any floor.

name: Quoits
blurb: Traditional target game tossing rope rings over numbered scoring poles.
includes: Carry case, 4 rope rings, wooden base halves, and 5 poles.
title: Quoits (Ring Toss) Hire | Pretoria & Johannesburg
description: Hire a quoits ring toss set with rope rings and a five-peg wooden base for parties and events in Pretoria and Johannesburg. R150 plus deposit.
intro: Quoits is the fairground ring toss: throw rope rings at a wooden base of numbered pegs and add up your score. It's quick, low-effort and works for every age at the party, from small children to grandparents in deck chairs.
The set comes in a carry case with four rope rings, a two-part wooden base and five scoring pegs.
surface: Any flat surface, indoors or out.
rules: Assemble the wooden base and stand the five pegs in it - the centre peg scores highest.
Mark a throwing line 2 to 4 metres away, closer for children.
Each player throws all four rings in turn.
Add up the values of the pegs you ringed.
Highest total after an agreed number of rounds wins.
faqs: Is quoits good for small children?
Ideal. Bring the throwing line close and it's an easy win for a four-year-old; move it back for the adults.
Can quoits be played indoors?
Yes - the base sits on any floor and the rope rings won't mark anything.
